notes: 'EventData/Data' holds key/value pairs: 37 keys are fields of their own through pairs ('user', 'event', 'action', 'by_user', 'item_id', 'folder' ...), each read as an extract entry would. The text itself isn't mapped (map it too, to Description say, if it's wanted whole). A key only one record shows is left out: add it the same way if it's wanted.

Set EventSource/System/Name and Environment to what the user confirms (or the standing instructions say). Both are required: if the user doesn't know one, use a placeholder they agree to (such as Unknown) and record it as an open item, rather than stopping.
'details' reads as each event's message, so it is EventDetail/Description, the event's own description: keep it there in every rule, rather than in an object's Description or a Data entry.

Drafted from the sample's values (check them): User: Authenticate for action Login, Login Failed; Authenticate for action Logout; Session: Process for action Start; System: Update for action Configuration Changed.

One rule per value of 'event' (Secret, User, Folder, Session, System, Permission): replace each EventDetail/Unknown left by the action element that describes the kind (Authenticate, Network, Process, View, Create, Update, Delete, Alert, Send, Receive...), and move its Data entries into that element (e.g. EventDetail/Alert/Data); 'other' catches the rest. Work through the schema problems build_translation_xslt reports: each names what the element takes. Unknown is for records no action element describes, not a way round a schema error; build_translation_xslt refuses it where the values show an action.

Set EventSource/System/Name and Environment to what the user confirms (or the standing instructions say). Both are required: if the user doesn't know one, use a placeholder they agree to (such as Unknown) and record it as an open item, rather than stopping.
Drafted from the sample's values (check them): User: Authenticate for action Login Failed, Login; Authenticate for action Logout.

One rule per value of 'event' (User, Secret): replace each EventDetail/Unknown left by the action element that describes the kind (Authenticate, Network, Process, View, Create, Update, Delete, Alert, Send, Receive...), and move its Data entries into that element (e.g. EventDetail/Alert/Data); 'other' catches the rest. Work through the schema problems build_translation_xslt reports: each names what the element takes. Unknown is for records no action element describes, not a way round a schema error; build_translation_xslt refuses it where the values show an action.

notes: 'EventData/Data' holds key/value pairs: 20 keys are fields of their own through pairs ('user', 'event', 'action', 'by_user', 'item_id', 'source_ip' ...), each read as an extract entry would. The text itself isn't mapped (map it too, to Description say, if it's wanted whole). A key only one record shows is left out: add it the same way if it's wanted.

Set EventSource/System/Name and Environment to what the user confirms (or the standing instructions say). Both are required: if the user doesn't know one, use a placeholder they agree to (such as Unknown) and record it as an open item, rather than stopping.
'details' reads as each event's message, so it is EventDetail/Description, the event's own description: keep it there in every rule, rather than in an object's Description or a Data entry.
Drafted from the sample's values (check them): User: Authenticate for action Login Failed, Login; Authenticate for action Logout.

One rule per value of 'event' (User, Secret): replace each EventDetail/Unknown left by the action element that describes the kind (Authenticate, Network, Process, View, Create, Update, Delete, Alert, Send, Receive...), and move its Data entries into that element (e.g. EventDetail/Alert/Data); 'other' catches the rest. Work through the schema problems build_translation_xslt reports: each names what the element takes. Unknown is for records no action element describes, not a way round a schema error; build_translation_xslt refuses it where the values show an action.

name: 48_jsonl_damaged_lines (excerpt)

notes: 1 of the 6 lines read aren't JSON objects (first: line 5, isn't JSON: Unterminated string starting at). Stroom's JSONParser stops the stream at the first such line, a fatal error, and every record after it is lost. Read the lines with a Data Splitter instead, one record a line (build_data_splitter spec {'kind': 'regex', 'pattern': '^(.*)$', 'names': ['json']}), and map their keys through json_fields: ['json'] (a key is then json.<key>): a line that isn't JSON gives no fields, matches no rule and is logged, and the rest are read.
